public_rationale: StarCoder supplies a documented counterexample to 'every single.' Its paper restricts pretraining to The Stack, and its repository documents code-generation and assistant applications available before the post. That recipe does not use Common Crawl. LLaMA's documentation does support the narrower observation that prominent models use Common Crawl alongside other sources. A supporting example cannot rescue a universal statement with a counterexample.
limitations: The result addresses the explicit universal scope, not whether web-derived training is common.
StarCoder is a specialized code LLM.
The result does not determine the legality of any training corpus.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Every single LLM-based application, including ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Anthropic's Claude and Meta's LLaMA, is trained on an indeterminately large portion of the internet made up of Common Crawl and what appears to be as much of the rest of the internet as they are able to download, legally or otherwise.

our_interpretation: The claim concerns the completed training of models underlying applications available by 2024-04-15. The historical training interval has no stated beginning.
I take 'every single' literally, including specialized LLM applications; the named products are examples, not an exclusive list.
The testable commitment is that each underlying model used Common Crawl and substantial additional internet material.
The hedged language does not supply a minimum corpus size or establish that every developer acted illegally.
criteria.support_condition: Training records establish the stated combination of Common Crawl and additional internet material for every application within scope.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented LLM application available before the post used an underlying model trained without Common Crawl or without the stated combination of sources.
